(b) NO REDUNDANT REF REBUILD, per the architect's ruling. decodePolicyWaiverRecord recomputes humanApprovalRef/waiverRef and the fold re-derives the aggregate id at leg :127 and enforces ref uniqueness at :128-129/:134, so a reader-local rebuild would be unreachable. The reader delegates and treats every corruption class the same way: zero events on an enumerated aggregate, any fold refusal (bad type, out-of-order sequence, tampered bytes, mismatched hash, foreign aggregate id) and any thrown store error all return POLICY_WAIVER_RECORD_UNREADABLE at literal DAEMON_POLICY_WAIVER.

(c) SUPERSESSION IS READER-OWNED AND STRUCTURALLY CANNOT TRUST THE FOLD'S FLAG. `candidate.superseded` is deliberately NOT carried into the reader's LoadedGrant type — the field does not exist in the reader's model, so trusting the lineage flag is impossible without editing the type. selectCurrent() walks the ordered survivors backwards and returns the LAST grant that is itself valid (not revoked, not expired); a predecessor is therefore displaced only by a successor that itself passes every join and every validity condition. When nothing is valid, the last survivor is current and reports its own refusal.

(d) DETERMINISTIC JOIN. JOIN_ORDER is a frozen 6-step array of {code, matches}: project -> principal -> action -> policyRevisionRef -> obligation -> scope, each filtering the survivor set and refusing with its own code on the first empty result. Scope is SET equality via two Sets compared by size and membership, so the same members in any order are the same scope. obligationRefusal() then counts occurrences of the named obligation across every slice's every rule's every obligation: zero -> OBLIGATION_FOREIGN; exactly one SOFT and no HARD -> pass; anything else (ambiguity or any HARD) -> NOT_SOFT.

(e) VALIDITY. Expiry lives in ONE comparator, isExpired() = `record.expiresAtEpochMs <= evaluatedAtEpochMs`, used both by the selection predicate and by the final check, so the equality boundary has a single production site to mutate in the drill. Revoked is checked before expired. Missing history (no aggregate, or no grants) -> RECORD_MISSING. The accepted result is Object.freeze({aggregateId, observedVersion, ok, waiver}) where waiver holds exactly the five canonical @moe/core PolicyWaiver fields, and aggregateId/observedVersion come from the same fold that produced those bytes.

(f) RAILS. Only the two owned production paths were created. Codec, leg, resolver, policy services, registry, core, store, manifests, lockfile and .moe are untouched. No branch mints, repairs, migrates, defaults or broadens authority; every refusal returns exactly {code, layer, ok} with no waiver, no aggregate id and no version.

TYPECHECK NOTE for whoever touches JOIN_ORDER: `Object.freeze([...] as const)` and `Object.freeze<T>([...])` both lose contextual typing for the predicate lambdas and produce TS7006 implicit-any on every parameter. The working shape is a typed `joinStep(code, matches)` factory whose parameter types give the lambdas their context, with Object.freeze applied to the outer array only.

implementationPlan.description:
MUTATION DRILLS (DoD 5). Four separate mutations, each reddening its OWN named assertion while all EARLIER guards are satisfied — that clause is what stops a drill from reddening because an upstream fence refused first.

Capture exact-path `git status --porcelain` first. The reader .ts/.js/.test.ts are NEW and UNTRACKED at drill time, so `git diff` on them certifies NOTHING — back each up out-of-tree under %TEMP% suffixed with your worker id and prove every restore by SHA-256 equality in a command SEPARATE from the restore. (DoD 5 says 'tracked restore is proven'; these paths only become tracked after landing, so use the SHA route until then.)

1. EXPIRY COMPARATOR: change `<=` to `<`. RED: the exact-equality EXPIRED arm. This is the only arm that catches it.
2. SCOPE SET-EQUALITY: make it positional/order-sensitive. RED: the same-set/different-order accepted arm.
3. SOFT UNIQUENESS GUARD: accept a non-unique or HARD occurrence. RED: the corresponding NOT_SOFT / OBLIGATION_FOREIGN arm.
4. SUPERSESSION SEMANTIC — the drill the governor asked for by name: flip the reader to trust the fold's `candidate.superseded` flag instead of evaluating successor validity. RED: BOTH trap arms from step 2 (successor-expired and successor-revoked). If this drill comes back GREEN, the validity-aware path is not actually exercised and that is a FINDING, not a pass.
5. REF RECOMPUTATION — **CHECK FOR VACUITY BEFORE BANKING IT.** decode and the fold already recompute the refs and the aggregate id, so a mutation to a reader-local copy may red only because the prerequisite refused first, which grades the prerequisite rather than this reader. Construct a fixture where the reader's own comparison is the ONLY mechanism that can refuse. If no such divergence input is constructible, say so plainly and report the clause as unprovable from inside this row's ownership — do NOT ship a drill whose red comes from an upstream fence.

Restore each mutation separately, prove the restore, and re-run green before the next.

WHAT LANDED. Supersession is READER-OWNED and VALIDITY-AWARE.     // Revocation ends authority, not lineage: the next grant still supersedes this predecessor.
    if (prior !== undefined) prior.superseded = true;
That is supersession by LINEAGE — any later grant marks its predecessor, including one that is later revoked or itself expired. The controlling amendment (comment-3179250312934a0ba29cf11e57fd2eb1) requires supersession by VALIDITY: "a later grant that is itself expired or revoked does NOT supersede." The two disagree, and the disagreement is observable, which is what drill 4 proves.
